title: "I am first and I am last": the whole chain in short, and the Aibershter mamash here
overview: Chapter 7 begins the second part of the book: after the chapters on what *hisbonenus* is, a general overview of the *hishtalshelus* it is done on, so that every particular learned later fits into the *klal*. From *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* after the *tzimtzum* to *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* it is one chain, and the end is wedged in the beginning: "I am first and I am last." Above the chain is the Essence before the *tzimtzum*; below it are we and the physical world, and it is *davka* there, in the bunnies of *Tehillim*, that the *Ein Sof* rests. A King is king at His borders, and every unification is only a *prat* before what is above it. The middle is transparent, like a phone line, and in the *Kesarim* it is all one will. For Rabbi Markel the point is that the *Aibershter* is *mamash* here, on the conference call. A last class talks freely about learning the book: *Shaar HaYichud* is a kindergarten book that shows you are a worm, and learning it takes *mesirus nefesh*, giving up the will to be a big shot.

sections.title: One chain from first to last: the point is that the Aibershter is mamash here
sections.summary: Chapter 7 opens the second part of the book with a general overview of the *hishtalshelus*, so that every particular learned later fits into the *klal*. From the first to the last it is one chain, "I am first and I am last", and the whole purpose of contemplating the particulars is to see that the *Aibershter* is *mamash* here, standing and listening.

phrases.he: (ז) ומעתה יש להקדים בתחלה
phrases.en: So first of all, we have to give you what the general overview is

phrases.he: וקודם להידיעה בפרטות כל ההשתלשלות ענין הנזכר לעיל (באות ד') בחיבור הפרט עם הכלל דווקא כו'
phrases.en: so that later on, when we tell you all the *pratim*, you'll know where it fits into the *klal*

blocks.text: Chapter 7 begins the book's second part: after what *hisbonenus* (contemplation) is and its introductions on *yesh* and *ayin*, the *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent) it contemplates. First, in this chapter, the general overview.
The *prat* (particular) has to be joined to the *klal* (whole), *davka*, so that each particular has its place.

phrases.he: בהיות ידוע לכל מעיין בספר הזוהר ובספרי הקבלה האמיתים
בהשתלשלות והתלבשות הפרצופים כו'
בסדר קצר ההכרחי לכל אדם לידע
מתחלה אחדות הפשוטה מריש כל דרגין
עד סוף כל דרגין בסוף עולם השפל שלנו
שהוא בא בחיבור וקשר אחד ממש
phrases.en: It's really all one connected thing; it's not a whole bunch of different things.

phrases.he: מראש לסוף ממש כשלשלת כו'
שמשתלשל מעילה לעילה כו'

blocks.text: The short order of what the *Zohar* and Kabbala describe, which everyone must know: from the simple unity to the end of our lowly world, it is one bond, *mamash*.

Many err here, thinking the *sefiros* are separate things. But *kol man d'afrish chad mechavrei*: whoever separates one *sefira* from another, it is as if he made a blemish in the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d).

phrases.he: ואור הראשון דאחדות הפשוט שנקרא עילת כל העילת
הוא הנקרא ראשון או קדמון
כמו שכתוב אני ראשון ואני אחרון
phrases.en: I'm the first, I'm the last.

phrases.he: אני ראשון הוא בחינת מלכות דאין סוף אחר הצמצום הראשון הנקרא מקום פנוי כו'
ואני אחרון סוף הכל הוא בחינת מלכות דמלכות דעשיה מקור התהוות זה העולם השפל
ונעוץ תחלתן בסופן וסופן בתחלתן
והיו לאחדים ממש
phrases.en: It's not two different things; it's *mamash* one thing,

phrases.he: כשלשלת
phrases.en: like a chain:

phrases.he: שהאחרונה ביותר קשורה בהעליונה ביותר
phrases.en: when you put a chain together, the end of the chain connects to the beginning.

blocks.text: The first light is called First: "I am first and I am last." First is *Malchus* (kingship) of the *Ein Sof* (the Infinite) after the first *tzimtzum* (contraction); last is *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* (the world of Action), the source of this world.

blocks.title: The chain and the necklace
blocks.text: Their beginning is wedged in their end, *mamash* one thing, **like a chain**: close it into a necklace and it is *davka* the end that touches the beginning, more than the middle links do.

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב ראו כי אני אני הוא,
phrases.en: You should see that the same One that I'm down here is the same One that I'm up there:

phrases.he: בלא שינוי
phrases.en: it's *mamash* no change

phrases.he: מראש לסוף כלל

blocks.text: "See that I, I am He": the One down here is the One up there, unchanged. That is the whole point; if it looks like two things, you are not getting it. *Chassidus* means that all the way down is *mamash* the *Aibershter*.

phrases.he: והגם שידוע שיש ריבוי פרטי השתלשלות מאד מאד
phrases.en: even though there's really many, many particular things in *hishtalshelus*

phrases.he: מראש לסוף,
הנה זה כל האדם
phrases.en: this is the whole thing, why you're here:

phrases.he: בהתבוננות כל פרטי פרטיות מראש לסוף,
phrases.en: the whole reason you have to do the *hisbonenus* of all the *pratim*,

phrases.he: לחבר הכל ליחוד הכללי דאחדות הפשוט הנקרא ראשון
phrases.en: to connect the whole thing to the *achdus pshuta* of the beginning of the whole thing.

blocks.text: The *hishtalshelus* has very many particulars, but this is the whole of man: you contemplate them all to connect the whole to the simple unity at its beginning, *ein od milvado* (there is nothing besides Him).

So if you are learning this like those people who learn Kabbala and want to know how to meditate on the *sefiros*, or to know which *sefira* is acting, "this is total baloney." It is not what it is all about. The whole *inyan* is that the *Aibershter* is here, *mamash* here, standing.

sensitivity.reason: Calls the way of those who study Kabbala to meditate on the sefiros "total baloney".
sensitivity.publishable: Learning this in order to know how to meditate on the *sefiros*, or to know which *sefira* is acting, is not what it is all about. The whole *inyan* is that the *Aibershter* is here, *mamash* here, standing.

blocks.text: One of the Rebbe's twelve *pesukim* says it: "And behold, G-d stands over him, and the whole earth is full of His glory; and He looks upon him and searches his kidneys and heart, whether he serves Him as is fitting." The *Aibershter* is standing here to see whether we serve Him one hundred percent, and the only way to that is *hisbonenus*.

blocks.title: The Aibershter on the conference call
blocks.text: *Hisbonenus* is not working out which *sefira*, or where to aim your *kavanos* (intentions): it means the *Aibershter* is standing here. This class is a conference call, and He is on it, listening closely to see whether we learn for Him or for some self-serving motive. He even looks into our *kishkes* (guts), *bochen klayos valev*: do we want the essential *tevuna*, or to cash in on it?

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב אני אני הוא ממש
phrases.en: It's *mamash*: the *Aibershter* is here.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב אני יהו״ה לא שניתי כו'

blocks.text: "I, I am He": the *Aibershter* is on this conference call the way I am here and you are here, and even more so.

blocks.title: With you in spirit
blocks.text: Not like the guest who sends word that he is with you in spirit. Then send the check! "Oh, the check is also there in spirit." The *Aibershter* is here like a physical thing, hearing every word.
"I, *Havaya*, have not changed": not some contraction of Him, but His very Essence and being, *atzmuso umahuso*, is down here on the call with us.

phrases.he: וזהו עיקר קוטב היסוד המוסד בהתבוננות הפרט דוקא,
שיומשך הכל אל הכלל כנזכר לעיל.

blocks.text: This is the pivot of contemplating the particular: drawing everything to the *klal*, to the *Aibershter* here.

sections.title: The short order: from He and His Name down to Malchus of Malchus of Asiya
sections.summary: Before the *tzimtzum* there was He and His light, filling a *chalal* that nobody asks about. Then came the *tzimtzum*, the *reshimu* and the *Kav*, and the chain in which each world's *Malchus* becomes the *Keser* of the next, down to *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, the end of G-dliness.

phrases.he: וביאור הדבר למתחילים,
phrases.en: So now, to explain this thing to the beginners:

phrases.he: הנה ידוע בדרך קצרה
phrases.en: now he's going to give us the short overview.

phrases.he: בסדר ריבוי השתלשלות דבחינת הקו וחוט שנמשך אחר צמצום הראשון,
הוא כך
phrases.en: This is how it is.

phrases.he: דבתחלה קודם הצמצום הראשון היה הוא ושמו בלבד כו'
phrases.en: Was just Him and the light.

phrases.he: דהיינו עצמיות אין סוף ברוך הוא ואורו וזיוו הנקרא שמו
phrases.en: There was the *Atzmus Ein Sof* and the *Or Ein Sof*, which is called His Name.

phrases.he: הכל היה בבחינת עצמיות שלו בבחינת אין סוף ממש,
והיה ממלא את כל החלל כו'
phrases.en: The *Ein Sof* and His light was filling up the whole *chalal*.

blocks.text: For beginners, the short order of the *Kav* (line) after the first *tzimtzum*. Before it was He and His Name alone: the Essence of the *Ein Sof* and the *Or Ein Sof* (the infinite light), called His Name.

blocks.question: "And it filled the whole chalal": what chalal? There was nothing but the Aibershter, so where did this space come from?
blocks.text: No one he has learned this with asks what *chalal* (space) this is: to them space is a given. So he suggests, *b'derech efshar* (as a possibility), that the *chalal* is higher than the *Atzmus* (the Essence), which apparently needs a place to be in.

phrases.he: ואחר כך צמצם את עצמו
ונשאר בחינת רשימו מן הצמצום שבחלל זה
ומרושם זה נמשך בחינת הקו וחוט בבחינת מקיף ופנימי כו'
ונקרא אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום בשם טהירו עילאה
ובחינת מקיף הכללי דקו זה בראשיתו נקרא טהירו תתאה כידוע

blocks.text: He contracted Himself, leaving a *reshimu* (impression) from which the *Kav* is drawn as *makif* (encompassing) and *pnimi* (inner) light. Before the *tzimtzum* is the *tehiru ila'a* (upper purity); the *Kav*'s *makif* is the *tehiru tata'a* (lower purity).

phrases.he: ואחר כך נמשך על ידי צמצום, מלכות דאין סוף להיות כתר דאדם קדמון
וממלכות דאדם קדמון נעשה כתר לעתיק יומין ואריך אנפין
וממלכות דאריך אנפין נעשה כתר לאבא ואמא
וממלכות דאבא ואמא נעשה כתר לזעיר אנפין ומזעיר אנפין לנוקבא
עד שממלכות דאצילות נעשה כתר לבריאה
וכך מבריאה ליצירה
phrases.en: And then the whole thing goes over again in *Beriya*: all these levels go over again in *Beriya*, till *Malchus* of *Beriya* becomes *Keser* of *Yetzira*;

phrases.he: ומיצירה לעשיה
עד בחינת מלכות שבמלכות דעשיה סוף הכל כו'
phrases.en: this keeps going all the way, to *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, the end of everything.

blocks.text: *Malchus* of each level becomes *Keser* (crown) of the next: of the *Ein Sof* to *Adam Kadmon*, then *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin*, *Abba*, *Ima*, *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*, until *Malchus* of *Atzilus* becomes *Keser* of *Beriya*; and again through *Yetzira* and *Asiya*.

blocks.question: "Down to Malchus of Malchus of Asiya, the end of everything": what do you mean, the end of everything? Where are we? Where do we fit in?
blocks.text: Where do we fit in? Not here yet: **the end of everything** means the end of *Elokus* (G-dliness). After it comes the world of the *kelipos* (husks).

sections.title: The end wedged in the beginning, and the two levels left out
sections.summary: *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya* is wedged in *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*: "I am first and I am last." The Essence before the *tzimtzum* is above beginning and end, and we are below the chain; and it is we who connect to the Essence, through the mitzvos.

phrases.he: ונמצא סוף הכל
phrases.en: The end of everything,

phrases.he: שהוא מלכות דמלכות דעשיה,
נעוץ בתחלת הכל שהוא בחינת מלכות דאין סוף שמתצמצם להיות כתר לאדם קדמון
כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים בהתחלתו בשער הכללים,
והיינו אני ראשון ואני אחרון כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: And this is what it means: *ani rishon*, *Malchus* of *Ein Sof*; *v'ani acharon*, *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*.

blocks.text: So the end, *Malchus* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, is wedged in the beginning, *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* becoming *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*, as at the start of *Etz Chaim*.

phrases.he: (מה שאין כן בחינת עצמות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום
לא נקרא עדיין גם בשם תחלה וסוף
כי הרי הוא בחינת אור עצמות עדיין כמו שהוא טרם שנמשך בשביל השפעה למטה
כמו שכתוב אתה קדוש ושמך קדוש כו' כידוע)
phrases.en: Both *Atah*, Himself, and the light are *kadosh*: totally removed, with nothing to do with all this *hishtalshelus*.

blocks.text: The Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum* is not yet called beginning or end, not yet drawn out to give below. So two levels are left out of the *hishtalshelus*: that Essence above it, and us below it.
Really it is we who connect to the *Atzmus* itself, through the mitzvos. "You are holy and Your Name is holy": He and His light are removed from the *hishtalshelus*.

sections.title: The two unifications of the Shema, and a King is made at the borders
sections.summary: Contemplating every particular from top to bottom draws it all up to the Essence before the *tzimtzum*: that is "*Havaya* is One", the *yichuda ila'a*. "Blessed be the Name" is the *yichuda tata'a*, one *Malchus* down to *Asiya*; and since a king is king at his borders, *Malchus* of *Asiya* is the biggest *Malchus*, and we push the border out by conquering the world for Him.

phrases.he: והנה אחר, היחוד
בהתבוננות היטב בכל פרטי ההשתלשלות מריש כל דרגין שהוא מלכות דאין סוף עד מלכות דעשיה דוקא,
phrases.en: Only when you look good and understand all the *pratim*, from the beginning to the end,

phrases.he: אזי יומשך הכל אל המקור הראשון
phrases.en: only then can you pull the whole thing even higher than *Malchus* of *Ein Sof* after the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת עצמיות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום

blocks.text: Only after understanding all the particulars, from beginning to end, can everything be drawn to its source, and even higher than *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* after the *tzimtzum*: to the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before it.

phrases.he: והיינו כוונה כללית דפסוק ראשון ביחודא עילאה דקריאת שמע
phrases.en: That's the *kavana* of the *Shema Yisrael*.

phrases.he: יהו״ה אחד,
אחדות פשוט ממש שלפני הצמצום הראשון,
שעל זה אמר בספר יצירה לפני אחד מה אתה סופר
phrases.en: What do you count before one?

phrases.he: למעלה מי׳ ספירות כו'
phrases.en: Higher than the ten *sefiros*.

phrases.he: וכמאמר אנת הוא חד ולא בחושבן י׳ ספירות כו' וכידוע
phrases.en: You are one, and not even in a *cheshbon* of ten *sefiros*.

blocks.text: The *kavana* of "*Havaya* is One" in the *Shema* is the simple unity before the *tzimtzum*: as *Sefer Yetzira* says, "Before one, what do you count?", above the ten *sefiros*. It is *Yachid* (the Singular): "You are One, and not in the count of the ten *sefiros*," as chapter 10 will explain.

phrases.he: וכוונה כללית דברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד ביחודא תתאה
הוא בחינת מלכות דאין סוף אחר הצמצום
שעל זה אמר מלכותך מלכות כל עולמים,
phrases.en: Your *Malchus* is *Malchus* of all the worlds,

phrases.he: עד מלכות דעשיה שהוא ענין אני ראשון ואני אחרון הנזכר לעיל

blocks.text: The *kavana* of "Blessed be the Name of the glory of His kingdom forever and ever," the *yichuda tata'a* (lower unification), is *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* after the *tzimtzum*: one *Malchus* of all worlds down to *Asiya*, as a king rules the same from Hodu to Kush. And *va'ed* is *echad*.

Not a great *Malchus* in *Atzilus* and lesser ones below: the same *Malchus*. Really *Malchus* of *Asiya* is bigger than *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, because in *Malchus* the external counts more than the internal.

blocks.title: The palace and the borders
blocks.text: A king grows by pushing out his borders, not by enlarging his palace. Achashverosh ruled "from Hodu till Kush," not Shushan; America runs from Canada to Mexico, not from Washington. The thing of *Malchus* is *davka* the borders.
So the biggest *Malchus* is *Malchus* of *Asiya*, the border. Up to it the *Aibershter* is uncontested King; past it, in the world of the *kelipos*, is a no-man's zone where His rule is contested.

blocks.title: Alsace-Lorraine and Kashmir
blocks.text: Like Alsace-Lorraine between Germany and France, or Kashmir today between Pakistan and India: each claims it. Here too the *Malchus* is not accepted.
He becomes a bigger King by pushing into the world of the *kelipos*. That is what we do now, conquering the world for the *Aibershter*; and what has to be conquered is not His yet.

blocks.question: What do you mean it is not His? Everything is His: "The earth and its fullness are G-d's."
blocks.text: Yes, but we are talking about a kingdom. The thing of a kingdom is that it has to be recognized.

blocks.title: Iraq: conquered, not consolidated
blocks.text: In this world there are rebel bands running around, as in Iraq, which Bush conquered but which has not yet been consolidated: it is not a real *Malchus*, the sovereignty is not recognized. And a *Malchus*, as opposed to a dictatorship, has to be recognized: the King has to be coronated *davka* by His subjects.

sensitivity.reason: A current-events example naming Bush's conquest of Iraq, which a public edition might read as a political remark.

blocks.text: So for now the *Malchus* runs from *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* to *Malchus* of *Asiya*: "I am first and I am last."

sections.title: Every unification is only a particular: the makif, the primordial thought, and Yachid
sections.summary: The whole joining of beginning and end is one *prat* within the *makif* that circles the *Kav*, the primordial thought; and that in turn is one *prat* before the Essence, which is not even a *klal* to a *prat*. From that *Yachid* the life of all the worlds is drawn.

phrases.he: וכל יחוד וחיבור דראש לסוף זה אחר ההתבוננות בפרטיות רבות שביניהם
אינו רק כמו פרט אחד לגבי בחינת הכלל הכוללם יחד
שהוא בחינת מקיף הכללי דעגול שמקיף לקו

blocks.text: Each unification of beginning and end is itself only one particular of the *klal*: the *makif* of the *igul* (circle) around the *Kav* of the *machshava kduma* (primordial thought).

blocks.title: One person in Pittsburgh
blocks.text: Any *yichud* is like that. I am one person in Pittsburgh, a city in the United States, in the world; the whole world, which we will take over, is a *prat* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, that of *Asiya*, that of the levels above, until all is a *prat* of the *machshava kduma*.

phrases.he: וגם הוא פרט אחד יחשב
phrases.en: The *machshava kduma* is only one *prat*

phrases.he: לגבי עצמיות אור אין סוף שלפני הצמצום שנקרא טהירו עילאה
שלמעלה מהיות גם בחינת כלל לפרט,
phrases.en: That's not even called a *klal* to a *prat*.

phrases.he: מאחר שנקרא קדוש ומובדל בבחינת העצמיות
phrases.en: It's totally separate from it, has nothing to do with it.

blocks.text: The *machshava kduma* too is only a *prat* to the Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum*, the *tehiru ila'a*, which is not even its *klal*: holy, separate from it.

phrases.he: וזהו פירוש יחיד חי העולמים
מבחינת יחיד זה נמשך על ידי צמצום הראשון הנזכר לעיל
להיות נקרא חי כל העולמים דאבי''ע שבקו בבחינת מקיף ופנימי כו'
וכידוע
phrases.en: As is known.

phrases.he: ודי למבין.

blocks.text: "*Yachid*, life of the worlds": from *Yachid*, through the *tzimtzum*, comes the *machshava kduma*, as *makif* and *pnimi*. That is the framework.

sections.title: Training the mind: the short out of the long, down to the physical
sections.summary: Once every particular is learned, a person trains his mind and heart all his life to make the short out of the long, until in one moment, from whatever he sees, he goes whoosh straight to the *Aibershter*. In the physical world itself, seen with physical eyes, the *Ein Sof* rests.

phrases.he: ואחר שיבואר לאדם ביאור כל פרט בסדר השתלשלות זאת,
הצריך לכל אדם לידע ולקבוע בנפשו
הנה תמיד כל ימי חייו
phrases.en: the whole time, every day of his life,

phrases.he: ירגיל מוחו ולבו
אחר טוב ידיעתו ורגילותו תמיד בכל פרטיהם דווקא
לעשות הקיצור מן האריכות מראש לסוף יחד
phrases.en: he should be *margil* himself to immediately see that the *Aibershter* is *mamash* here.

blocks.text: Once the particulars are explained, he must train his mind and heart every day to make the short out of the long, until he sees immediately that the *Aibershter* is here.

blocks.question: So why not go like that right away, and just say the Aibershter is here and the Aibershter is here?
blocks.text: That is a main complaint. The answer is the Alter Rebbe's about the maid: she says it but does not know it; it is an image in her head, with no concept behind it.

phrases.he: עד שברגע א' ממש בהתבונן בנפשו בסוף הכל,
phrases.en: Whenever he sees whatever happened, immediately he can put the whole thing together in one shot,

phrases.he: שהוא השגות איכות התהוות יש מאין הגשם דגלגלים וד' יסודות הגשמיים וכל פרטי עולם הזה השפל

blocks.text: Until in one moment, seeing the *galgalim* (celestial orbits), the four elements or any detail of this world, he goes in one shot through the *Ofanim* (angels), *Asiya*, *Yetzira*, *Beriya*, *Atzilus*: whoosh, the *Aibershter*. A hurricane, food that tasted real good: the *Aibershter* did it.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב שאו מרום עיניכם,
בראיה גשמיית,
וראו מי ברא אלה,
phrases.en: and see who created these things

phrases.he: בגשמיות התהוותם ליש גמור ממש בצמצום היותר אחרון
שבזה ממש שורה בבחינת אין סוף דוקא
phrases.en: But in the *gashmiyus*, when he sees the *gashmiyus* in front of him, in that is the *Ein Sof*, *davka*

phrases.he: מבחינת תחלת הכל, שהוא בחינת מלכות דאין סוף שלפני מקור האצי'

blocks.text: "Lift up your eyes on high," with physical sight: the *re'iya* (sight) *Moshiach* will bring, when tasting your food is tasting the *Aibershter*. "**and see who created these**," in their very physicality, at the last *tzimtzum*.
Before he went only to *Malchus* of *Asiya*; now he brings in the physical: in what a person sees in front of him rests the *Ein Sof*, *davka*, the beginning of everything.

sections.title: Why Tehillim praises the bunnies: the middle is transparent
sections.summary: *Tehillim* praises G-d for bunnies and boats and not for angels, because the real thing of the *Aibershter* is *davka* down here. All the levels in between are like a phone line, transparent; and one must want to know the particulars, as a fan or a friend does, because ignoring Someone who is standing right there is the biggest insult.

phrases.he: וע"כ לא נזכר בכל ספר תהלים בשבחי גדולת יהו״ה רק בדרך פשוט,
בגדולות ונפלאות מעשה יהו״ה בשמים וארץ וכל צבאם הגשמיים דוקא
ולא נזכר שבחי גדולתו בעולמות העליונים רוחניים
phrases.en: It doesn't talk about the angels and stuff like that in *Tehillim*.

phrases.he: עד רום המעלות שלפני האצילות כו'

blocks.question: Bunnies are the praise of G-d?
blocks.text: *Tehillim* praises G-d simply: a rock for each bunny, the lions roaring, boats on the sea. On a tiny planet, what praise is that? Just the opposite: that the *Aibershter* gives each bunny a rock to hide under, "that's where you see the actual *Atzmus*."

Nor does *Tehillim* praise Him through the angels or the levels before *Atzilus*, only "You helped me with my enemy": the beginning is wedged in the end, and down here, "I, I am He," is the real thing of the *Aibershter*.
*Malchus* spreads beyond its borders: spreading down past *Asiya*, it spreads upward too, to the *Atzmus* before the *tzimtzum*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 054 opens, before it reads line 49, by finishing the point the previous tape was making about the borders of the Malchus (lines 33-34) and the physical world below them (lines 46-48); placed after the end of class 053.

blocks.title: The balloon
blocks.text: Like a balloon: blow it up and both sides grow. In the end the *sovev* comes from there.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 054 opens, before it reads line 49, by finishing the point the previous tape was making about the borders of the Malchus (lines 33-34) and the physical world below them (lines 46-48); placed after the end of class 053.

phrases.he: מפני שנעוץ תחלתן בסופן דוקא כנזכר לעיל
וכמו שכתוב אני אני הוא ממש וכו'
phrases.en: *Mamash*: I am Him, right here. With us.

phrases.he: ועצמיות אור אין סוף הוא הסובב כו'
phrases.en: The *Atzmus Ein Sof* is the actual *sovev* on the whole thing.

phrases.he: ודי למבין.
וזהו אמיתית המכוון בהתבוננות בפרט כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: And that's the real *amitiyus* in the *kavanos* of *hisbonenus bifrat*, as mentioned above

blocks.text: The *Atzmus* of the *Ein Sof* is the *sovev* (the encompassing) on the whole. That is the truth of contemplating the particulars: *davka* through them you see the *Aibershter* is here.

phrases.he: (וגם שלפי החשבון בפרטי ההשתלשלות, רחוק מאד מאד מראש לסוף,
phrases.en: It looks very far.

phrases.he: אבל באמת קרוב מאד בלי הפסק והסתר כלל באמצע
phrases.en: It's really totally close, without no *hefsek* at all.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב אני אני הוא
phrases.en: It's *mamash* Me. I am right here, I'm right here with you.

phrases.he: ומבלעדי באמצעיתא כו'
phrases.en: And beside Me, in the middle, there's nothing.

phrases.he: ודי למבין)

blocks.text: Counted by its particulars it is very far; in truth it is close, with no break in the middle.

blocks.title: The phone line
blocks.text: The middle is like the phone line between us: however long, we discount it and talk as if the other is here. It is transparent.
So every connection in the middle of the *hishtalshelus* is transparent and discounted: "I, I am He." I am at the beginning and I am at the end, and the middle is not there.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב כי האלהי״ם עשה את האדם קדמאה ראשית הקו, ישר מראשו לסופו
phrases.en: The *Aibershter* made *Adam Kadmon* totally straight

phrases.he: עד עקב דאדם קדמון שמסתיים בסוף העשיה בבחינת יושר
שהוא ההתכללות גמור מראשו לסופו,
והמה בקשו חשבונות רבים בבחינת העגולים כו'
בפירוד והתחלקות זה למעלה מזה כו')

blocks.text: "For G-d made man straight": *Adam Kadmon* is one straight line, poof, to the end of *Asiya*. Take it simply, the *Aibershter* is here, so much that you can forget the *hisbonenus*: *al daas hatinok hazeh* (by the mind of this child), as the Rebbe said.

blocks.question: So what do you need all this hisbonenus for? Why all the complications?
blocks.text: Why not be the Baal Shem Tov's simple Jew with his whistle, believing like a baby that the *Aibershter* is here? But "they sought many reckonings": people do not see straight. If I put my money in an IRA, by 65... What does anything have to do with that?
As a mitzva, live on a budget as the *Rambam* says, but do not believe in it. So, first: without *hisbonenus* there is no real *emuna* (faith) that the *Aibershter* is here.

blocks.title: The fan club
blocks.text: Second: what is real to you, you want in detail. Fans of Michael Jackson or the Beatles want everything, not just the music; Elvis, *l'havdil*, is dead for years and they want to know his hotel. If the *Aibershter* were standing with you as your friend, you would want to know all about Him.

blocks.title: Meeting a new guy
blocks.text: Meet a new guy you want as a friend, and you ask where he is from, what he does, whether he is married. Interest means wanting the details; not wanting the *Aibershter*'s means no interest in Him.

Then you have nothing to do with Him; worse, it is an insult. Not believing at least is not ignoring Him. But He is standing right there, wanting to know everything about you, and you will not even say hello: "the biggest insult you can have."

sections.title: In the Kesarim there is no distance: one will, from the simple will to the will to do
sections.summary: In the *Kesarim* there is no cause and effect with a distance of levels: from the simple will, still *hiyuli*, through the will to emanate and to create, down to the will to make, it is one will, as in a person who wants to walk and walks. A free discussion follows on how this book is to be learned: it is a kindergarten book, and it shows you that you are a worm.

phrases.he: ויובן כל הנזכר לעיל בדרך קצרה מאד בבחינת הכתרים שבכל עולם
שאין בכתרים בחינת השתלשלות עילה ועלול בריחוק המדרגה כלל
phrases.en: By the *Kesarim*, there's no real *hispashtus*.

phrases.he: כמו בחינת הרצון הפשוט שבעצמיות אור אין סוף,
כמו שכתוב כשעלה ברצונו הפשוט כו',
בחינת מלכות דאין סוף עצמה כשעלה במחשבה הפשוטה אנא אמלוך כו'
שהוא למעלה מרצון להאציל או לברוא כו'
רק בחינת היולי עדיין

blocks.text: In the *Kesarim* (crowns) there is no spreading, no cause and effect at a distance. It is like *Ana Emloch* (I shall rule) arising in His simple will, *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof* itself: no will to emanate or create yet, only *hiyuli* (raw potential).

phrases.he: וממנו נתצמצם תחילה בחינת רצון הקדום שנקרא כתר לאדם קדמון
ואחר כך הרצון להאציל, בחינת כתר דאצילות בכלל
ואחר כך הרצון לברוא, בחינת כתר שבמלכות דבריאה,
ואחר כך כתר מלכות דיצירה כו'
עד כתר מלכות דעשיה, הרצון לעשות
וכמו שכתוב כל אשר חפץ יהו״ה עשה כו'
phrases.en: What He wanted, that's what He did.

blocks.text: From it came the primordial will, *Keser* of *Adam Kadmon*; the will to emanate, *Keser* of *Atzilus*; the will to create; down to *Keser* of *Malchus* of *Asiya*, the will to make. "All that G-d desired, He did": one continuum. A person, too, thinks because he wants to do.

phrases.he: ומהו ההפרש באדם התחתון בבחינת רצונו ועצמותו ההיולי
שהיה כלול בו ד' רצונות
כמו רצון לעצמות גופו לרצון לפעול ולעשות היותר אחרון,
הכל משרש ומקור אחד יצא כו'
phrases.en: it's all the same *ratzon*.

phrases.he: כך אין הפרש ממש בין בחינת רצונו הפשוט שנמשך להיות רצון להאציל,
phrases.en: So it's *mamash* one thing.

phrases.he: לבחינת רצונו הפשוט שנמשך להיות חפץ יהו״ה בכל אשר עשה בסוף עולם העשיה שלנו כו' ודי למבין

blocks.text: In man, the *hiyuli* will includes all his wills, from his body to the last act: one root. Just so His simple will, drawn down to emanate and to all He did at the end of *Asiya*, is *mamash* one thing.

blocks.title: Walking without thinking about the nerves
blocks.text: With us it is the same. A lot goes on between brain and mouth, but you do not think about it. Whoever thinks, as he walks, which nerve and muscle to move will fall over. He wants to walk: poof, he walks.

blocks.title: The widths of lengths
blocks.text: The width (*rochav*) of three lengths (*orech*) takes more than the three lengths. Two stones build two houses: a width of two needs only its lengths. With three come the three lengths, the three widths of two, and, before the width of three, how each width of two connects with the others: not six things but nine, more like permutations than combinations. Without those connections you do not have the full width of three.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 reads no line: it is a free discussion, picking up a discussion of lengths and widths of understanding from an earlier class, on how this book is to be learned. Its blocks are placed under the chapter's last passage. Its strongest tie is to line 43, "to make the short out of the long": a length is learned point by point and then held in the head in one shot (055 w912-942).

blocks.text: And that is only three. With four come single, double and triple lengths, and how each connects with each: how do one-two-three connect with three-four? The more lengths, the more complicated the width.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: And it is all automatic, like the garment of *or* with an *aleph* (light) and with an *ayin* (skin) discussed before: both garments, *mamash* the same garment.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.title: A fifth-grade explanation for a second-grader
blocks.text: A garment with an *ayin* is an explanation too deep for you, fifth grade taught to a second-grader: it leaves him more confused than before.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: And besides that, they try to make *chiddushim* (new insights), to tie together one thing they learned in *Ayin Beis* with another thing they learned in *Torah Or* and a *sicha* (talk) of the Rebbe, without realizing that they might be talking about different things: different lengths, different explanations. And they really do not even have the length, the *hisbonenus* of the one simple length, because they started out with fifth grade instead of with kindergarten.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

sensitivity.reason: Mocks an identifiable kind of student in his own community, who strings together Ayin Beis, Torah Or and the Rebbe's talks without understanding any of them.
sensitivity.publishable: A person may try to make *chiddushim* (new insights), to tie together one thing he learned in *Ayin Beis* with another thing he learned in *Torah Or* and a *sicha* (talk) of the Rebbe, without realizing that they might be talking about different things: different lengths, different explanations. And he may not even have the length, the *hisbonenus* of the one simple length, because he started out with fifth grade instead of with kindergarten.

blocks.text: That is what the key means: what comes before first grade. *Shaarei Orah* is the *aleph-beis*; the key comes before it, the basic code before first principles.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: *Ayin Beis* is hard to keep in your head as a whole length. A length is all its points held in one shot; a width is all the lines held together as a plane, which presupposes the length. Separate points are not even a length, and without the length there is no width.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: So what they have is only points, points, without the whole length. And even if you try to teach these people a simple explanation from *Shaar HaYichud*, they will try to relate it to what it says in *Ayin Beis*: they want to do a width. But they do not understand the length there, nor the length here, and they already want to be on a width.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

sensitivity.reason: Continues the mockery of "these people" who want to relate Shaar HaYichud to Ayin Beis without understanding either.
sensitivity.publishable: If what you have is only points, points, without the whole length, then when you learn a simple explanation from *Shaar HaYichud* you will try to relate it to what it says in *Ayin Beis*: you want to do a width. But you do not yet understand the length there, nor the length here, and you already want to be on a width.

blocks.text: *Shaar HaYichud* is a kindergarten book, keys that get you used to learning at all, like nursery, where kids paint an *aleph* and sing before the *aleph-beis*. Grasp the length of *Ayin Beis*, and surely you understand this.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: In the olden days they said not to study Kabbala and *Chassidus*, because it will mix you up. You will make dark from the light and light from the dark, and you will end up doing like Shabsai Tzvi and becoming a Muslim, G-d forbid. Or even if you stay a Jew, you will mix it all up in your head, and you will have a Judaism that is really *avoda zara* (idolatry), "which most people do have."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

sensitivity.reason: Treats becoming a Muslim as the end of the road to ruin, and says that most people's Judaism is really idolatry.
sensitivity.publishable: In the olden days they said not to study Kabbala and *Chassidus*, because it will mix you up. You will make dark from the light and light from the dark, and you could end up like Shabsai Tzvi, G-d forbid. Or even if you stay a Jew, you will mix it all up in your head, and you will have a Judaism that is really *avoda zara* (idolatry).

blocks.title: The child who found an aleph
blocks.text: Like a small child catching on to letters: you are reading *Ayin Beis* or a *Chumash*, and he points: "Oh, look, an *aleph*!" He knows it as well as you, but not the word, the sentence or the *inyan*. Then he finds another; to the reader they are different *alephs*, in different words of different *inyanim*.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: Over there it is the same: they can talk of a *helem* (concealment) in existence and one not in existence, and *hispashtus min ha'etzem* (spreading from the essence), but that is a letter, with no idea how it fits. This small book shows the confusion that there stays hidden.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: This book mentions the two kinds of *helem* in passing, and you do not see why. There five chapters on one *helem* feel understood, but they belong to fifty on some *inyan*, themselves a *prat*. This is a letter, the fifty a word: you never reached a sentence. Like understanding "the". "The" what?
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.title: Any book will do
blocks.text: Their understanding is points, like the child's: whatever page, whatever book, *Imrei Bina* or *Yedios Achronos*, he finds an *aleph* and a *beis* he knows and is delighted.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: It makes no difference to him: it could be *Imrei Bina*, *Chovos HaLevavos* or *Yedios Achronos*, or a book by Gershom Scholem, which is total heresy: here is an *aleph* and here is a *beis*, *mamash* the same thing.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

sensitivity.reason: Calls the books of a named recent scholar, Gershom Scholem, "a total heresy".

blocks.text: Here you see the *alephs* and *beises* connect. This book shows you are not a human being: till you learn it you have no *machshava iyunis* (analytical thought). It tells you you are a beast; learn a little, and "Wait a minute, it's not even a beast."
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.title: A worm on your hand
blocks.text: As David HaMelech says, "I am a worm and not a man." A dog cannot go to college, but knows a smile and a wagging tail get a cookie. A worm on your hand does not know it is a hand, and is not even scared, as a squirrel is. Here it tells you you are a worm.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

blocks.text: This is yesterday's subject, the inwardness of the Essence. Learning *Chassidus*, as chapter 6 ended, takes *mesirus nefesh* (self-sacrifice), giving up your *ratzon* (will), for *nefesh* means *ratzon*; and your *ratzon* is to be a big shot.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 055 (free discussion), placed under the chapter's last passage.

reviewQuestions.question: Why does the chapter give a general overview before the particulars, and what does the chain show about the *sefiros*?
What is the whole purpose of contemplating all the particulars, and what does the conference call have to do with it?
Which two levels does the order of *hishtalshelus* leave out, and where are they brought back in?
Why is *Malchus* of *Asiya* the biggest *Malchus*, and how does the King become a bigger King?
Why does *Tehillim* praise G-d for the bunnies and not for the angels?
If the *Aibershter* is simply here, what is all the *hisbonenus* for? Give both reasons.
